entities.evidence: נֹחַ is the son of Lamech who survived the flood and planted a vineyard after leaving the ark.

analysis.evidence: The next clause, וַיִּטַּע כָּרֶם, tells what Noah did as a man of the soil: he planted a vineyard. This supports the Hiphil sense “begin.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with Noah as its subject.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: נֹחַ names the subject of וַיָּחֶל. The phrase אִישׁ הָאֲדָמָה describes Noah as a man of the soil, and וַיִּטַּע כָּרֶם says he planted a vineyard.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אִישׁ הָאֲדָמָה, “man of the soil,” the following noun completes the construct phrase and identifies Noah as a farmer. His planting a vineyard supports this occupational sense.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: man of …: one marked by a quality, calling or people

analysis.evidence: Noah is called אִישׁ הָאֲדָמָה, “a man of the soil.” His planting a vineyard (וַיִּטַּע כָּרֶם) shows that the phrase refers to the ground he cultivates.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state. The noun completes the construct phrase אִישׁ הָאֲדָמָה.
analysis.sense: the ground that is tilled; soil

analysis.evidence: כָּרֶם, “a vineyard,” is the direct object of וַיִּטַּע and identifies what Noah planted.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with Noah as its subject. The initial נ of the root assimilates to ט, marked by the dagesh.

analysis.evidence: כָּרֶם is the direct object of וַיִּטַּע, “he planted.” The clause says that Noah planted a vineyard.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of both genders, singular absolute. The initial qamats is the pausal vowel at verse end. The word has no prefix or suffix.
